keyRules: Maximum height: 120 m (400 ft) AGL (ANAC); recreational flights: no more than 60 m (200 ft) AGL (DECEA, ICA 100-40)
Drones weighing more than 250g: mandatory registration with SISANT (ANAC)

Drones up to 250 g do not need to be registered with SISANT (ANAC Resolution No. 806). Since 1 July 2026 (ICA 100-40), flights also require authorization through SARPAS (DECEA) for these drones. Drones over 250 g must be registered with SISANT.

Airport Flight Restriction Zones (FRZ) (ICA 100-40, in force since 1 July 2026): around the aerodrome (ZEA), the FRZ starts at ground level out to 1,740 m; you stay below it by flying up to 100 ft (30 m) beyond 1,740 m, 200 ft (60 m) beyond 2,350 m, 300 ft beyond 2,960 m and 400 ft beyond 3,570 m. In the approach and take-off sectors (ZAD), the FRZ starts at ground level out to 3,550 m; after that: 100 ft beyond 3,550 m, 200 ft beyond 4,480 m, 300 ft beyond 5,400 m and 400 ft beyond 6,320 m. Flying inside the FRZ requires a Termo de Coordenação and a SARPAS request at least 4 calendar days in advance.
Recreational flights (ICA 100-40, art. 32): maximum height of 200 ft (60 m) AGL and maximum horizontal distance of 300 m. Near aerodromes, the FRZ bands apply – check in SARPAS.
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS)
Minimum distance of 30 m from people not involved in the operation

Every flight requires airspace access authorization through SARPAS (DECEA), including drones up to 250 g. Minimum advance notice: 30 minutes in the open category; 4 or 8 calendar days for operations intersecting an FRZ or restricted areas, BVLOS or above 400 ft. Recreational flights in an EAC designated for recreation are exempt.
Transmission equipment must be certified by ANATEL
Night flights: the drone must have navigation lights (ICA 100-40, art. 20)
Pilots under 18 must always be accompanied by a pilot over 18 who is responsible for the operation

Non-recreational use of drones over 250 g (RBAC No. 100): insurance covering third-party damage is mandatory. Passing the ANAC theory exam (RBAC 100.13(b)) is waived until 31 December 2026 (Resolution No. 805/2026, art. 2).
importantNotes: Tourists: Brazil ALLOWS recreational flights. Drones over 250 g must be registered with SISANT (foreigners can use their passport), and flights require SARPAS (DECEA) authorization, including with drones up to 250 g.

ANAC fines for drones start from reference amounts of R$ 750 to R$ 4,500 per violation (operating without registration: R$ 2,250 – Resolution No. 762/2024); depending on mitigating and aggravating factors, the final amount can range from 20% to 300% of that amount (Resolution No. 761/2024, art. 35). Flying without SARPAS authorization is an air traffic violation judged by the JJAER (ICA 100-40, art. 66).
National parks (ICMBio) and indigenous areas (FUNAI) generally prohibit drones without specific authorization
Beaches and urban tourist areas (Rio, São Paulo, Salvador) have municipal restrictions—check with local authorities

fields.disclaimerText: Always consult the official sources from ANAC and DECEA before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. Brazil applies RBAC No. 100 and Resolution No. 806 (ANAC, since June 2026) and ICA 100-40 (DECEA, since July 2026), with mandatory authorization through SARPAS.
